subject: Re: Pilot extension — add days vs graded discount proposal
messages:
From: Emma Torres <emma@infralabs.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot extension ask — options?

Hi Priya,

Quick one — the engineering team needs a little more runway on the Redwood pilot. We’re close to a production proof point but need an extra 2–3 weeks to finish integration and load testing. Finance is sensitive to giving a hard-dollar top-up right now.

Two asks: can you (a) add 21 days to the current timebox (same cap/throughput) or (b) offer a short-term graded discount on overage usage for the next 30 days (e.g., 25% off above the current cap up to an extra 200k tokens)?

We’re evaluating both operational simplicity and the path to conversion. If there’s a hybrid you think is fair, tell me. Will need procurement signal quickly so we can loop legal if needed.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Torres
Head of Platform Engineering | Infralabs
emma@infralabs.ai

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Torres <emma@infralabs.ai>, Carlos Velasquez <carlos@infralabs.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot extension ask — options?

Emma — thanks for the clear options. Really glad to hear integration is close. I put together two concrete paths so your procurement/legal teams can pick the least friction route: attached is a short proposal and an addendum draft.

Option A — Timebox extension (operationally simplest)
- 21 additional calendar days added to the current pilot
- Same throughput caps and artifact retention
- No invoice or payment change; we convert remaining days into a one-time credit if you sign a paid commitment within 30 days of pilot end

Option B — Graded overage discount (billing-first alternative)
- Pilot window extended by 30 days for overage pricing only
- 25% rebate on overage units between current cap and +200k tokens
- Rebate applied as credit towards first paid invoice if you convert within 60 days

Hybrid suggestion (A+B) — 14-day extension + 15% overage credit up to 150k tokens, with a conversion credit if you commit within 45 days. This reduces legal friction while giving you operational runway.

Next steps: if you prefer Option A we can push an addendum (no PO required). If Finance prefers Option B we’ll need a brief billing addendum and a PO/commitment trigger for the rebate. I’ve cc’d a draft SOW addendum in case you want to circulate to procurement.

I’ll hold on any approvals until I hear which path you want to move forward with.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.ai
Attachment: infralabs_pilot_proposal_v2.pdf

Folks — looping you in for quick pricing and legal guidance. Infralabs (prospect) asked for either 21 days added or a graded overage discount. Attached is the proposal I plan to send; want to minimize credit risk but stay competitive.

Questions:
1) If we offered Option A (21 days) versus Option B (25% rebate to +200k tokens), which has the lower revenue risk while keeping the deal warm?
2) Is a hybrid (14 days + 15% to 150k) acceptable from finance/legal?

Can you reply with bullet guidance — need to respond to the customer by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Priya

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot extension ask — options? (pricing guidance)

Quick numbers/policy:
- Option A (21 days): Lowest billable risk. We’re not changing price per unit; we’re just extending time. Recommend if customer is near conversion and the usage profile is predictable. No rebate bookkeeping.
- Option B (25% rebate to +200k): Medium risk. Rebate creates credit liability and will require a PO or conversion trigger to limit exposure. Use if procurement insists on no contract amendment.
- Hybrid (14d + 15% to 150k): Good compromise — reduces run rate exposure and signals we’re invested without full credit liability. Approve from finance side if we cap total credit liability to $X (internal cap noted in separate doc).

Operational notes:
- If we do Option A, operations can flip the pilot end date on our side; legal addendum is minimal (signature + effective date).
- If Option B / Hybrid, require an explicit conversion trigger (signed commitment or PO) to release rebate credit — otherwise we reserve the right to convert credits into invoice offsets over 12 months.

Recommend we offer the hybrid publicly: 14 days + 15% rebate up to 150k tokens, with rebate applied only if Infralabs signs a paid order within 45 days. That should be acceptable to procurement and keeps legal paperwork light.

-Markus

Subject: Pilot extension — our compromise proposal

Emma / Carlos — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on internal guidance here’s a single, short option that should minimize both procurement friction and billing risk.

Our offer (one-line): 14 additional calendar days + a 15% rebate on overage units up to 150,000 tokens; rebate becomes a one-time credit if you sign a paid order within 45 days of the new pilot end date.

What this means practically:
- Pilot end date extended 14 days from your current termination date (no change to caps/throughput).
- Any tokens above your current cap during the extended window are eligible for a 15% rebate, capped at 150k tokens.
- Rebate applied as credit to your first invoice if you convert within 45 days; otherwise, credits will expire (or convert to an invoice offset under standard terms).

Attached: short proposal (infralabs_pilot_proposal_v2.pdf) and the draft SOW addendum (SOW-addendum-draft.docx) for procurement/legal to review. If you’re good with the hybrid, I can generate a slim addendum and a DocuSign link for signature — no PO required to sign the addendum, but a PO is required to trigger any billing changes.

Next step: tell me if you want me to send the DocuSign now or if procurement prefers to review the attached SOW first. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call to walk through.

Best,
